boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten public, no-purchase activities on or near Northwestern’s Evanston campus, each supported by a direct source.

cards.entity_name: Mary and Leigh Block Museum of Art Galleries
cards.title: Look through the Block galleries
cards.subtitle: 40 Arts Circle Drive · Evanston campus
cards.notes: Meet during public gallery hours, pick one work each, then compare what you noticed before moving to the next room.
cards.short_summary: A free public gallery visit with three exhibition spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The Block Museum states that it is free and open to all and describes three galleries.
cards.access_notes: Public gallery hours vary by season; the visit page posts current hours and closures.

cards.title: Catch up at Block Spot
cards.subtitle: Block Museum · 40 Arts Circle Drive
cards.notes: Use the counter along the windows for a conversation break, then step into the galleries if they are open.
cards.short_summary: A light-filled conversation area inside the free Block Museum.
cards.evidence_claim: The Block’s visit page identifies Block Spot as an interior counter for conversation and states the museum is free and open to all.
cards.access_notes: Located inside the Block; visit during posted museum access hours.

cards.title: Walk the sculpture garden
cards.subtitle: Block Museum · 40 Arts Circle Drive
cards.notes: Take a slow lap through the outdoor works, choose a favorite detail, and use it as a prompt for a photo-free sketch or chat.
cards.short_summary: Outdoor art beside Northwestern’s Arts Circle.
cards.evidence_claim: The Block identifies a sculpture garden and outdoor artworks around Northwestern’s Arts Circle; the museum is free and open to all.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor works are around the Arts Circle; check the museum’s visit guidance for site conditions.

cards.title: See what’s up at Dittmar
cards.subtitle: Norris University Center · 1999 Campus Drive
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition notice, walk the rotating display together, and pause to discuss one piece that invites a closer look.
cards.short_summary: A public gallery in Norris with rotating exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwestern states that Dittmar Gallery admission is free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Dittmar Gallery exhibits ‘The Story of Ka Makana O’ Ka’
cards.access_notes: Gallery availability can change during exhibition installation; confirm building and gallery access before going.

cards.title: Browse the first-floor Noyes show
cards.subtitle: Noyes Cultural Arts Center · 927 Noyes Street
cards.notes: Start with the first-floor display, take in the work at an unhurried pace, and compare a detail each person wants to remember.
cards.short_summary: Free art viewing on the first floor of Noyes Cultural Arts Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Evanston lists the Noyes Art Gallery on the first and second floors and states that admission is free.
cards.access_notes: City-posted gallery hours are Monday through Friday, 10 a.m.–6 p.m.

cards.title: Continue upstairs at Noyes
cards.subtitle: Noyes Cultural Arts Center · 927 Noyes Street
cards.notes: Use the second-floor gallery as a separate stop: choose one work to describe aloud before checking the exhibition information together.
cards.short_summary: A second-floor, no-admission art stop at Noyes.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Evanston lists the Noyes Art Gallery on the first and second floors and states that admission is free.
cards.access_notes: City-posted gallery hours are Monday through Friday, 10 a.m.–6 p.m.

cards.title: Pull a local-history thread
cards.subtitle: Dawes House · 225 Greenwood Street
cards.notes: Plan a research-room visit with a question in mind, then compare the local records or images each person finds most revealing.
cards.short_summary: A free research-room visit at the Evanston History Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Evanston History Center lists Research Room admission as free and gives public research-room hours.
cards.access_notes: The research room is listed Tuesday–Thursday and Saturday, 1–4 p.m.; check for holiday closures.

cards.title: Look through Dearborn’s telescope
cards.subtitle: Dearborn Observatory · 2131 Tech Drive
cards.notes: Reserve the first-hour slot or arrive for second-hour walk-in viewing, and dress for an unheated, non-air-conditioned dome.
cards.short_summary: Free Friday-night public telescope viewing in spring and summer.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwestern states that Friday public viewing runs 9–11 p.m. in April–September, is free and open to all, with second-hour walk-ins welcome.
cards.source_title: Friday Nights at the Dearborn Observatory
cards.access_notes: Friday viewing is 9–11 p.m. during April–September. Reservations are required for the first hour; the second hour accepts walk-ins. Not ADA-accessible.

cards.title: Save a seat for CIERA’s public lecture
cards.subtitle: Cahn Auditorium · 600 Emerson Street · October 8, 2026
cards.notes: Bring a friend for the evening lecture and check the event page nearer the date for program details or any updated logistics.
cards.short_summary: A scheduled, free public astronomy lecture at Cahn Auditorium.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwestern lists CIERA’s October 8, 2026 Annual Public Lecture at Cahn Auditorium as free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled for October 8, 2026, 7–8 p.m. CT; consult the event page for updates.

cards.title: Tour Silverman Hall’s science cores
cards.subtitle: Silverman Hall · 2170 Campus Drive · October 1, 2026
cards.notes: Meet at Silverman Hall for the scheduled crawl, talk with core staff, and use the first- and third-floor stops to explore research tools together.
cards.short_summary: A free public walkthrough of Northwestern life-science core facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: Northwestern lists the October 1, 2026 CLP Core Crawl in Silverman Hall as free and open to students and the public.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled for October 1, 2026, 3–5 p.m. CT on the first and third floors of Silverman Hall.
